blocks.text: One time at a time: set the clock, then say the next one, as long as you like. Every time here is made from dictionary forms by the rules on the first page.

exercises.prompt: Set the clock to this time.
exercises.context: Past the hour: the minutes, then the NEXT hour as an ordinal in the genitive — «пять минут третьего».
exercises.why: «The moment the minute hand moves beyond the full hour, it begins to denote time in terms of some fraction of the following hour. Thus, “five minutes past two” is rendered in Russian by «пять минут третьего» (lit. “five minutes of the third”). Note that “the following hour” is always denoted by an ORDINAL numeral in the Genitive case.» «пятнадцать минут десятого — or — четверть десятого». — DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 74.

exercises.prompt: Write this time in words, the way it is said (пять минут третьего). You may leave off утра / дня / вечера / ночи. The 24-hour way (четырнадцать ноль пять) counts too.
exercises.context: Before the hour: «без» + the minutes in the genitive, then the next hour — «без пяти три».
exercises.why: «The moment the minute hand crosses the half-hour mark, it begins to denote time in terms of some fraction lacking for the completion of the next full hour. Thus, “five (minutes) to three” is rendered in Russian by «без пяти (минут) три». Note that the preposition «без» takes the Genitive case. The hour is rendered as a CARDINAL numeral and the word “minutes” is often omitted.» «без пятнадцати двенадцать — or — без четверти двенадцать». — DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 74. «The 24-hour system. Transportation, radio and military installations use the 24-hour system: Самолёт вылетел в 14.00 (четырнадцать ноль ноль). Командир будет здесь в 17.30 (семнадцать тридцать).» — DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 73.

exercises.prompt: Set the clock to this time.
exercises.context: On the hour: «два часа»; and утра / дня / вечера / ночи instead of AM and PM.
exercises.why: «Time on the hour: Сейчас два часа. Я приехал туда в два часа. (в + Acc.)» Instead of AM or PM Russians say «of the morning» (утра), «of the day» (дня), «of the evening» (вечера), «of the night» (ночи). — DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lessons 40 and 73.
